identity.title: Mitochondrial-lipid crosstalk and pharmacological intervention in HPDL deficiency.

content.abstract: The 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase-like protein (HPDL) converts 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate into 4-hydroxymandelate (4-HMA), an intermediate in an alternative pathway for the generation of 4-hydroxybenzoate (4-HB), a precursor of the Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) headgroup. However, the pathogenic mechanism of HPDL-related encephalopathy and related phenotypes such as spastic paraplegia (SPG83) remains unclear. In this study, we generated an hpdl(-/-) zebrafish model using the CRISPR/Cas9 methodology. Larvae exhibited microphthalmia, impaired yolk absorption, and a transition from hypokinetic-like to epilepsy-like activity. For the first time in HPDL-related research, we performed extensive lipidomic profiling, revealing a depletion of di- and triglycerides and cholesterol esters alongside mitochondrial membrane instability, marked by decreased acylcarnitines and increased dilysocardiolipins and hydroxy-acylcarnitines, a signature suggestive of impaired beta-oxidation and oxidative damage. Bypass and antioxidant therapies using 4-HMA, 4-HB, and the mitochondrial-targeted scavenger MitoTempo were evaluated for their rescue potential. While almost all of the tested drugs successfully rescued the reactive oxygen species production, brain cell death and the altered neuronal activity, we observed that the metabolic recovery occurred independently of the levels of CoQ10 and CoQ9, which remained depleted. Our findings offer support to the hypothesis that Hpdl deficiency causes disease primarily through mitochondrial redox imbalance and lipid metabolic failure, rather than a simple CoQ10 depletion. In spite of unchanged CoQ10 levels, rescue of oxidative stress, brain cell death, and neuronal hyperexcitability in mutant larvae by 4-HMA, 4-HB, and MitoTempo supports a cytoprotective role for these aromatic metabolites, identifies HPDL as a key regulator of mitochondrial homeostasis, and a promising target for aromatic antioxidant therapy.
